For Small Island Developing States 🏝️, the energy transition is not just about reforming energy systems. It is about economic stability, climate resilience, and national sovereignty. With renewables now cheaper than fossil fuels across most island grids, clean energy is no longer a cost—it is the smartest macro-economic choice.

Many #SIDS import the vast majority of their energy through fossil fuels. Around 60% import at least 90% of their energy, and in countries like the Maldives, fuel imports absorb more than 10% of GDP, reaching up to 16% across SIDS in some years. This dependence exposes economies to price volatility, supply disruptions, and extreme weather.

At the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Assembly, I discussed how SIDS are not waiting to transition — they are already leading it. Out of necessity and innovation, they are building power systems designed for climate resilience, energy independence, and the water-energy-food nexus, from solar-powered desalination to resilient island microgrids.

The real bottleneck today is not technology — it is finance. What SIDS need are bankable investment pathways that combine concessional capital, guarantees, and risk-sharing instruments to crowd in private investors at scale. This is where digital# data and #AI become transformative: by improving demand forecasting, data transparency, grid management, and real-time performance tracking, they reduce uncertainty, lower the cost of capital, and turn small, fragmented projects into investable portfolios.

So the question is no longer whether SIDS should transition.
It is how fast we can align #finance, guarantees, and digital intelligence to unlock clean-energy investments that match their ambition — and their urgency.
